output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error, not to the fungicide, Meridane or Lower Serra. The new documentation suite (Tallis) created the mandarin product record on 1 Aug by copying the avocado record, and the 7.0°C avocado carriage temperature stayed in it. All five Meridane containers booked through Tallis were set to 7.0°C, and the controllers held that temperature. Mandarins need 4.0°C. All five of those containers were rejected, with 9–14% decay. Every container shipped at 4.0°C passed, including Pellacor-treated fruit (K5, K7) and Meridane's K1 on the old email booking. K3 used old fungicide stock and still failed, which clears the new fungicide. Meridane followed the instructions it was given, so a claim would likely fail. Suspending Lower Serra would punish the wrong party. Their fruit looked worse within the rejected containers, but that is a secondary effect and not proven as a cause. Next steps: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4.0°C now. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification before submission. Review how the 3 Aug sign-off missed this. Hold off on claims, suspensions and the fungicide reversal. Confidence is high.
